children: BKV shares fell in premarket trading Wednesday after the company said it plans to raise $400 million by way of a notes offering.
Shares fell 6.6% ahead of the morning bell to $25.00.
The energy company said it intends to offer the $400 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due in 2031 in a private offering to eligible purchasers.
Purchasers will also be given the option to purchase up to an additional $60 million principal amount of notes, it said.
BKV plans to use the new money to repurchase its stock and to enter into the capped call transactions which aim to reduce the potential dilution of its shares when any notes are converted to stock.
The remainder is earmarked for general corporate purposes and debt repayment.
